papers.title_en: Refining Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation via Regional Semantics and Visual Prototypes
papers.authors: Aijing Yu, Zhengbo Wang, Lijun Sheng, Jian Liang, Xiao-Yu Zhang
papers.evidence: 引入区域语义的开放词汇语义分割
papers.tldr: CLIP在图像级开放词汇分类表现强，但用于像素级语义分割时区域与文本对齐不足。本文调整CLIP视觉编码器注意力层，以选择性注意力特征保留区域语义，并引入置信patch特征构成的视觉原型辅助分类器，结合可优化特征提取器与EMA更新。在5个语义分割数据集上实验验证了方法有效性，为开放词汇分割提供更精细的区域语义与原型细化思路。
papers.abstract_en: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) has shown superior performance in the image-level open-vocabulary classification task, benefiting from its powerful alignment of visual features and text embeddings. However, dense prediction tasks require models to perform pixel-level predictions, necessitating modifications to CLIP for region-text alignment. In this paper, we adjust the attention layers within the vanilla visual encoder of CLIP. With a novel attention calculation method for selective attention features, the model retains more regional semantic information. To further mitigate the negative impact of the modality gap, we introduce additional visual prototypes to refine the original predictor solely based on text embeddings. Specifically, patch features with confident predictions are selected to form an additional auxiliary memory-based classifier for more accurate prediction. We further integrate an optimizable feature extractor with an exponential moving average updating strategy to enhance prediction quality. Extensive experiments on $5$ semantic segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

papers.title_en: OV-Foam: How 3D Representations Shape Semantic Feature Lifting
papers.authors: Yousef Rajeh, Alejandra Esparza Pelcastre, Ivan Viola, Dominik Engel
papers.evidence: 基于PowerFoam表示的开放词汇分割特征提升
papers.tldr: 现有开放词汇分割常用反投影将特征分配给图元，但在3DGS中图元重叠严重、每射线图元过多，导致分配次优。OV-Foam改用PowerFoam作为底层表示，以power diagram划分场景，使图元零重叠并显著减少每条射线上的图元数量。这样将特征提升简化为更接近最优的分配问题，空间划分图元达到近最优赋值。实验表明其在开放词汇分割上优于Gaussian基线，说明3D表示结构直接影响语义特征提升效果。
papers.abstract_en: Existing feature lifting approaches for open-vocabulary segmentation rely on simple backprojection to assign features to primitives. In the case of 3D Gaussian splatting reconstruction, the primitives overlap heavily, leading to suboptimal reconstructions, governed by many primitives per ray. Backprojection, however, reduces to a least-squares solvable problem, exactly when no two primitives share a ray. Motivated by this insight, we propose OV-Foam, which uses PowerFoam as the underlying representation. This representation uses a power-diagram to partition the scene, resulting in zero overlap between primitives and a substantial reduction in primitives per ray, which ultimately simplifies the lifting problem and allows for closer-to-optimal feature assignment. We show that the space partitioning primitives of OV-Foam reach near-optimal assignment, and our experiments demonstrate improved open-vocabulary segmentation over Gaussian baselines.
